answer: Neighborhood-Spread Admission. An agent must be reachable through a growing frontier of prior peers, so admission spreads like a tide across the graph rather than through any credential. Each new node needs k distinct multi-hop paths from established regions; a clone arriving alone adds no edges, and padding it with fake neighbors is caught because those neighbors must themselves hold real paths. The cost per identity is the edge-maintenance work of sustaining k live routes through a lotus of honest clusters, which a meadow of disposable accounts cannot fake without genuine sustained traffic.
